title: Neuromatch Academy: NeuroAI (course book)
authors: Neuromatch Academy (course content team; per-tutorial content creators are named on each tutorial page)
description: Two-week intensive NeuroAI course published as a MyST book, organised around the question of which principles natural and artificial intelligence share ('The core challenge of intelligence is generalization.'). Days: W1D1 Generalization, W1D2 Comparing Tasks, W1D3 Comparing Artificial and Biological Networks (Foundations); W1D4 Project Day; W1D5 Microcircuits, W2D1 Macrocircuits, W2D2 Neuro Symbolic Methods (Architectures); W2D3 Microlearning, W2D4 Macrolearning (Learning); W2D5 Mysteries. Each day has an intro video, one to five Python/PyTorch tutorials with videos and coding exercises (Colab and Kaggle launch buttons), pod discussions and project time; a project booklet accompanies the course.
codeLicence: BSD 3-Clause ('Software elements are additionally licensed under the BSD (3-Clause) License', repository README; LICENSE-CODE.md 'Copyright 2020 Neuromatch Academy', read 2026-10-31)
rightsNotes: Content licence, repository README of neuromatch/NeuroAI_Course (read 2026-10-31): 'The contents of this repository are shared under under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License.' (the doubled 'under' is in the source). LICENSE.md is the CC BY 4.0 legal code ('Attribution 4.0 International'). The README adds: 'Derivative works may use the license that is more appropriate to the relevant context.'

The MyST book pages opened carry no licence footer (only 'Made with MyST'); the licence is taken from the repository, whose README names the book as the main access route: 'The content should primarily be accessed from our ebook: https://neuroai.neuromatch.io/ [under continuous development]'.

Datasets and pretrained models loaded inside tutorials (for example TrOCR in W1D1 Tutorial 1) carry their own terms and were not audited. Corniversity links to the tutorials rather than redistributing them, credits Neuromatch Academy and the named content creators, and issues no Neuromatch certificate.

W1D1 Tutorial 1 'Generalization in AI' (Samuele Bolotta and Patrick Mineault; estimated 75 minutes): handwriting recognition with TrOCR, measuring out-of-distribution generalization, dissecting TrOCR, generalization via augmentation and synthetic data
W1D2 Tutorial 1 'Task definition, application, relations and impacts on generalization' (Deying Song, Leila Wehbe; 90 minutes): tasks as cost functions (classification, regression, auto-encoder)

W1D3 Tutorials: T1 'Generalization and representational geometry' (RDMs; 40 minutes), T2 'Computation as transformation of representational geometries' (40 minutes), T3 'Statistical inference on representational geometries' (RSA model comparison, two-factor bootstrap; 50 minutes); the sidebar also lists (Bonus) T4 'Representational geometry & noise' and T5 'Dynamical Similarity Analysis (DSA)'

limitations: High entry requirement: the course expects the Neuromatch Computational Neuroscience and Deep Learning courses or equivalent plus intermediate Python; in Corniversity it follows NEU-220 (neuromatch-compneuro) and CSA-210 (neuromatch-deep-learning).
The schedule is a two-week intensive (two 90-minute tutorial blocks plus three hours of project time per day); it is not an evening-study workload estimate and must be re-paced.
Only the tutorial pages listed were opened; W1D5 and W2D1-W2D5 are known from the schedule and materials.yml only and have no page-level locators.
Embedded videos were not watched; no video timestamps are recorded.
No per-page version stamp; MyST page paths such as /w1d3-tutorial3/ were observed on 2026-10-31 and may change in a rebuild.
Tutorial pages exceed 100,000 characters; W1D1 T1, W1D2 T1 and W1D3 T2 were read in part, so their section lists may be incomplete.
